stepAnswer: They are kept separate by the placental barrier
stepExplanation: Maternal and fetal blood do NOT mix. They are separated by the placental barrier (thin membrane). Substances diffuse across this barrier between the two blood supplies. This protects the fetus from some harmful substances and immune rejection.
stepBody: How are maternal and fetal blood related in the placenta?
choices: They are kept separate by the placental barrier
Only fetal blood flows through the placenta
Only maternal blood flows through the placenta
